subject: Cardinal Data — edge appliance & on-prem connectivity plan
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lewis <samantha.lewis@cardinaldata.com>, Tom Brooks <tom.brooks@cardinaldata.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Cardinal Data — edge appliance & on-prem connectivity plan

Hi Samantha / Tom,

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our onboarding checklist, we want to lock the network plan for the Private deployment before we schedule the appliance shipment and on-site install. High-level asks for the preflight: 

- Confirm the desired VPC peering vs. private endpoint path (you mentioned peering + static routes on the call).
- Provide the CIDR blocks you want peered and any overlapping ranges to avoid.
- Confirm if the edge appliance will sit in a DMZ/network segment with an outbound proxy (some customers require proxy + strict egress rules).
- Any change-window constraints for firewall/peering config (we try to do switchovers in a 4-hour window).

I'll attach a short preflight checklist and an install stub for the appliance. Can you share your network diagram (layer 3) and a sample config for the NAT/static route you'd like us to use?

Proposed next steps:
1) You share network diagram + CIDRs by EOD Wed 2026-01-07.
2) We review and propose exact firewall rules + peering config by Fri 2026-01-09.
3) Technical review call the week of Jan 12 to sign off and schedule shipment.

If that timeline looks good, I'll schedule the review and loop in Mina and the install team.

Thanks,

Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai
Attachments: redwood-network-preflight-checklist.pdf, redwood-edge-appliance-install-stub.txt
From: Samantha Lewis <samantha.lewis@cardinaldata.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Brooks <tom.brooks@cardinaldata.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Jan 2026 12:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cardinal Data — edge appliance & on-prem connectivity plan

Alex — thanks, this looks good. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- We intend to use VPC peering (primary) and fall back to private endpoint if peering runs into policy constraints.
- CIDRs: corporate VPC (10.10.0.0/16), analytics VPC (10.20.0.0/16). We have subnets for ")edge" appliances planned in 10.10.200.0/24.
- We do use an outbound proxy for all outbound traffic from the DMZ; the appliance will need proxy egress credentials OR allowlist IPs for outbound to Redwood's ingestion endpoints.
- Preferred change window: Tue–Thu 02:00–06:00 PT.

We'll pull together a network diagram and a sample static route config and send by Wednesday. Also, do you support an air-gapped install mode? Some of our security folks asked if the appliance can be provisioned without direct internet during initial boot.

Regards,
Samantha Lewis
Head of Infrastructure, Cardinal Data
samantha.lewis@cardinaldata.com

Subject: Re: Cardinal Data — edge appliance & on-prem connectivity plan

Samantha — great, thanks for the quick reply. Short answers up front: yes, we support an air-gapped provisioning mode (it requires a short physical handoff and a pre-seeded config bundle), and we can either accept proxy credentials or provide a small set of fixed egress IPs for allowlisting.

I've attached the preflight checklist and an appliance install stub that documents the air-gap flow and proxy options. Action items from our side:
- Alex: propose exact firewall rules + peering config (by Fri 2026-01-09).
- Monica: validate appliance sizing and on-site install crew availability for Jan 20–26 window.
- Vivek: confirm egress IPs + certificate pinning requirements with infra team.

Can you confirm the proxy type (explicit proxy vs transparent) and if you require mutual TLS to Redwood endpoints? If mTLS is required we'll need to exchange certs ahead of the technical review.

Thanks — attaching: redwood-network-preflight-checklist.pdf, redwood-edge-appliance-install-stub.txt

--
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 7 Jan 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: INTERNAL: Cardinal Data preflight assignments

Team — internal checklist / notes (do not forward to customer):

- Monica: confirm Jan 20–26 install crew and co-lo access process (owner: Monica). Deliverable: install ETA + engineer names by 2026-01-09 EOD.
- Vivek: generate the static egress IP list and confirm we can support explicit proxy auth flow or certificate-based mTLS. Deliverable: egress IPs + mTLS support matrix by 2026-01-09 EOD.
- Mina: validate that our appliance image supports air-gapped initial config; coordinate a small pre-seed package we can ship on USB. Deliverable: pre-seed package instructions and verification checklist by 2026-01-11.
- Alex: prepare peering firewall rule set and sample BGP/static route snippet for their network team.

I'll draft the technical review agenda once we have their diagram. Keep items short and call out any blockers.

Alex
From: Tom Brooks <tom.brooks@cardinaldata.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Samantha Lewis <samantha.lewis@cardinaldata.com>
Cc: Cardinal Data Networking <networking@cardinaldata.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 8 Jan 2026 09:41:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cardinal Data — edge appliance & on-prem connectivity plan

Alex / Team,

Attached is the network diagram and our sample config. Key points:
- CIDRs confirmed: 10.10.0.0/16 (corp), 10.20.0.0/16 (analytics). Edge appliance will be in 10.10.200.0/24.
- We require explicit proxy auth (squid) for outbound from the DMZ.
- We cannot open inbound ports except for our internal management IPs; all control-plane comms should originate from the appliance to Redwood.
- We will accept an allowlist of static Redwood egress IPs for certificate fetching during initial bootstrap if an air-gapped option is not feasible.

Attachment: cardinal_network_config.yaml

We prefer the tech review on Tue Jan 13 10:00 PT if that's available for your team. Confirm and send a calendar invite and any pre-read.

- Tom

Samantha / Tom — thanks for the diagram and config. Quick summary and next steps before the tech review on Tue Jan 13 10:00 PT: 

What we understand (please confirm):
- VPC peering is primary; appliance in 10.10.200.0/24 will egress via explicit proxy (Squid).
- CIDRs: 10.10.0.0/16 and 10.20.0.0/16. No overlap with Redwood-managed ranges.
- Control plane: outbound-only from appliance; we will provide 3 static egress IPs to allowlist for bootstrap + certificate retrieval.
- Air-gapped: we will prepare a pre-seed USB bundle as an alternative if allowlisting is not approved by security.

Prework for the call (links):
- Network preflight checklist: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aB2cD-Cardinal-OnPrem-Prep

Mina / Vivek / Monica — we have the Jan 13 slot confirmed. Please join 10 minutes early to run through the pre-seed steps (Mina) and the firewall + peering snippets (Vivek).

Tom / Samantha — I'll send the calendar invite and attach the appliance install stub. Looking forward to the review.

Best,
